card.intuition: Each token has a finite amount of influence to distribute across the rest of the context, so heavy influence on one relationship leaves less for the others. The budget is per token and does not grow when the context does — your instruction stays the same strength while every other token competes, so the signal-to-noise ratio drops as the context grows.
card.analogy: A speaker with a fixed-volume microphone in a room that keeps filling up. The speaker never gets quieter — the words are character for character identical — but as the crowd grows the signal drowns. A louder mic (re-pasting) helps only briefly; the real fix is clearing people out of the room.
card.time_complexity: O(C squared) per request over the full context window — attention pairs every token with every other, so the per-request cost grows superlinearly with deeper context.
card.space_complexity: Context/memory footprint: the attention budget is per token and finite, so long or heavily loaded contexts dilute attention to earlier content as more tokens compete for the fixed influence.
when_to_use: Diagnosing 'why does it keep ignoring the schema I pasted at the top?' as a competing-signal problem, not plain disobedience
Keeping the window small: content that does not serve the task is noise over everything that does
Clearing when the accumulated context stops paying for itself, and restating the constraints that matter instead of trusting their early mention to hold
Choosing what enters context: you control the window, so prioritize signal over volume
gotchas: The symptom reads as disobedience — the agent agreed early then drifted; re-pasting the constraint adds another competitor and helps only briefly
The instruction never gets quieter; the room gets louder around it, which is the same mechanism as attention degradation
The budget cannot be extended — only the contents of the window are within your control

steps.label: Per-token fixed influence
steps.annotation: Each token has a finite amount of influence to distribute, and it does not grow when the context does.

steps.label: Signal at fixed volume
steps.annotation: Your instruction stays exactly as strong, character for character, no matter how large the context gets.

steps.label: Room gets louder
steps.annotation: Every extra token competes, so an instruction that was the loudest thing at 10k tokens is background hum at 150k.

steps.label: Reads as disobedience
steps.annotation: The agent agreed to a constraint early then drifts from it; the cause is the rest of the window, not the instruction.

steps.label: Keep the window small
steps.annotation: Control what enters context: clear when it stops paying for itself and restate the constraints that matter.

exercise.prompt: Compute the signal-to-noise ratio of an instruction when every token in context competes for the fixed attention budget.
hints: The noise is the number of competing tokens currently in the window.
Use the length of the context_tokens list as the competition term.
exercise.test_code:
assert signal_share(1.0, ['noise'] * 9) == 0.1
assert signal_share(1.0, []) == 1.0
assert signal_share(2.0, ['noise']) == 2.0 / 3.0
print('PASS')
